claims.text: `evict_oldest` looped over the inclusive range `0..=n`, so it attempted n+1 removals for a request of n entries.

It used `if let Some(oldest)` around `pop_front`, so an exhausted queue silently produced no-op iterations rather than ending the loop, and the method returned nothing to tell the caller how many entries had actually gone.
`Cache::put` computed `overflow` and called `evict_oldest(overflow + 1)` when the map had reached `max_entries`.
`evict` loops over the half-open range `0..n`, removing at most n entries rather than n+1.
The `pop_front` result is now matched explicitly and a `None` arm breaks the loop, so eviction stops as soon as the order queue is empty.

citations.item: pub fn kvstore::cache::Cache::evict(&mut self, usize) -> usize

claims.text: The method counts each successful removal and returns that count, so callers can observe how many entries were actually evicted; the doc comment states this as "returning how many were removed".
A new `capacity` accessor returns `max_entries`, documented as "The configured maximum number of entries"; it sits alongside the pre-existing `free_slots`, which reports remaining free capacity.
`Cache::put` keeps the same `overflow + 1` argument, now passed to `evict`, and discards the returned count.
Removing the public inherent method `Cache::evict_oldest` was flagged by cargo-semver-checks as `inherent_method_missing` at major level, making the required version bump for `kvstore` major.
The `evict_oldest` symbol is gone from `kvstore/src/cache.rs` and two new symbols, `evict` and `capacity`, appear in the same file.
The call edge from `Cache::put` to `evict_oldest` disappeared and was replaced by a call edge from `Cache::put` to `evict`.

The structural diff treats `evict` as a likely rename of `evict_oldest` (confidence 0.75), on the basis of the same file and overlapping source range with name similarity 0.59 — no symbol changed file in this change.
`handle_request` reaches the changed code through `Cache::put` and could be affected; it calls `cache.put` on the `put` verb path.
`kvstore/src/api.rs` imports the `cache` module and could be affected.
`kvstore/src/lib.rs` imports the `cache` module and could be affected.

These are possibilities, not certainties: the impact set is bounded reverse reachability over calls and imports at one hop, and states that a listed symbol depending on something the change altered is not the same as being broken by it.

Eviction volume through `put` changed silently: `put` still passes `overflow + 1`, but the callee now removes at most that many entries instead of one more, so each overflowing `put` evicts one fewer entry than before. Whether `overflow + 1` is still the right argument now that the off-by-one in the loop is gone is the main thing to verify.
`put` ignores the newly returned count, so a partial eviction — the queue emptying before n removals — is not observed at the only in-tree call site.

claims.text: The removal of a public method is a breaking change for external callers: any downstream user of `Cache::evict_oldest` must be migrated to `Cache::evict`, and the package needs a major version bump.

`capacity` and the existing `free_slots` are two adjacent public accessors over `max_entries` with different meanings — the configured maximum versus the unused remainder — which is worth checking for naming confusion at call sites.

output.summary: Renames `Cache::evict_oldest` to `Cache::evict` and changes its contract: it now removes at most `n` entries instead of `n+1`, stops cleanly when the queue runs dry, and returns the number actually removed. A new `Cache::capacity` accessor exposes the configured maximum entry count. `Cache::put` was updated to call the new method. Because a public inherent method was removed, cargo-semver-checks classifies this as a major bump for the `kvstore` package.
